 Live .  15,846 viewing 15846 viewing Dawson takes four as England complete 55-run win over Sri Lanka - reaction
 Thu 29 Oct 2026 , Men's One Day International Series Sri Lanka vs England, result Sri Lanka Sri Lanka Result England England 331 all out ( 45.1 ) 386 -5 ( 50.0 ) England   win by 55 runs Sri Lanka innings: 331 all out from 45.1 overs
 England innings: 386 for 5 from 50.0 overs
 Duckett and Dawson deliver in England's consolation win 
 Live Reporting (active) 
 Scorecard 
 Summary
 England end tri-series with consolation win - report 
 Four wickets for Dawson and two for Baker
 Rathnayake falls for 118 after giving SL hope
 Dangerous Kusal (89) removed by Root
 Duckett hits 167, his second century in two games
 Banton 74, Brook 44, Cox 43
 Close form Have your say on England men this winter
 Get involved What information do we collect from this quiz? Live Reporting
 by Mike Peter
 Post published at 16:28 GMT 16:28 GMT 
 Alex Hartley 
Former England bowler on Test Match Special 
 On where Harry Brook's captaincy is at... 
 I think it is hard to know. I think he is brilliant. I like his aggressiveness. 
 A few moments throughout this tour, I have not agreed with his bowling changes, but saying that he has not got the bowling changes that he would want or normally has. 
 I don't think you can blame England's performances on his captaincy. 
 2 1 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 get involved Get Involved published at 16:26 GMT 16:26 GMT 
 Click 'Get Involved' at the top of this page to have your say 
 In my view, we have been on the wrong side of results. England have actually played well this series without our premier quick (Archer) and spin (Rashid) bowlers. Add Buttler, Salt, etc back into the batting line-up and we are in rude health.
 Mark L, London 
 Phew a win at last! But nothing on it. England need to learn how to win meaningful matches with something on it!
 Neville F, Dorset 
 Granted the results haven’t been great. But three of these England games have been thrilling! It’s kinda like supporting Newcastle in the 90s! You’re not gonna win anything, but what a ride!
 Jade, Newcastle 
 7 2 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 16:23 GMT 16:23 GMT 
 Jonathan Agnew 
BBC Chief Cricket Commentator on Test Match Special 
 On England's bowling attack... 
 I don't think Harry Brook is quite sure.
 I think he is still trying to work out what bowling formula sort of works.
 Sam Curran has bowled a lot, certainly in the first couple of games. He has leant on him a lot. The Henry Crocombe thing today - I am not sure what that is all about.
 One minute he is bowling a vital over the other day, and then he just bowls three overs here.
 Like anything, Brook is learning captaincy. He is learning generally about bowling changes and the team that he wants around him.
 He has got time, and he has got a year until the World Cup.

Former England fast bowler on BBC Test Match Special 
 Image source, Reuters I just think if your top six batters do their job, as they did today, and with the guys who can bowl and bat, I think then playing the extra bowler can give you more firepower through the middle of the innings and then safety at the death.

 Post published at 16:17 GMT 16:17 GMT 
 Jonathan Agnew 
BBC Chief Cricket Commentator on Test Match Special 
 The batsmen score runs, the bowlers have an off day. 
 It hasn't all gelled together, so there is work to be done. Definitely as far as the make-up of the team.
 Adil Rashid's situation is an interesting one. Michael Vaughan has messaged asking why he isn't in the team?

 Alex Hartley 
Former England bowler on Test Match Special 
 Image source, Getty Images England found themselves on the wrong ends of results, so they can hold their heads high. 
 Three losses on the bounce would have been one too many.

 Post published at 16:11 GMT 16:11 GMT 
 Steven Finn 
Former England fast bowler on BBC Test Match Special 
 There would have been moments in the match when England were worried. 
 At the halfway stage England would have been content with where they were at. 
 There were some worrying signs through the middle that England couldn't take a wicket. 
 The bowling looked the same at times, but they hung in there and broke into those partnerships.

 Post published at 16:08 GMT 16:08 GMT 
 Alex Hartley 
Former England bowler on Test Match Special 
 That run out that wasn't from Pavan Rathnayake didn't end up being match costly. 
 England can breathe a sigh of relief. 
 England will be disappointed how this tournament has gone and gutted by the way it has gone. 
 Ultimately, they have got away with a win, and have a little bit of confidence leading into Australia.

 Post published at 16:05 GMT 16:05 GMT 
 Jonathan Agnew 
BBC Chief Cricket Commentator on Test Match Special 
 England finish the series with a token win. 
 To have come here and lost every game would have been a shambles.
 197 23 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 England win by 55 runs published at 45.1 overs 45.1 overs Breaking 
 Malinga b Curran 1 (SL 331 all out) 
 Image source, Getty Images Two wickets in two balls - Sam Curran wraps it up!
 Eshan Malinga takes a big swing at the seamer's opening delivery and has his leg stump pegged back.
 Having looked in trouble a few overs ago, they've taken 5-16 from 17 balls to ultimately win by a comfortable margin.
 344 8 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 16:05 GMT 16:05 GMT 
 Alex Hartley 
Former England bowler on Test Match Special 
 Brilliant catch from Tom Banton. Banton, running in shouts 'mine'. 
 It is an easier catch for him to take. Liam Dawson missed out on that first game, but he has come back and taken wicket after wicket.
 111 18 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 WICKET published at 45 overs 45 overs 
 Fernando c Banton b Dawson 1 (SL 331-9) 
 A second wicket in the over for Liam Dawson and his first four-wicket haul in ODI cricket!
 New batter Asitha Fernando tries to slam the England spinner down the ground and Tom Banton runs behind the wicket from long-on, sliding over the on-field advertising to take the catch.
 Dawson finishes with figures of 4-49 and England are one wicket away from a consolation win in this tri-series.
 297 6 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 15:59 GMT 15:59 GMT 
 Jonathan Agnew 
BBC Chief Cricket Commentator on Test Match Special 
 That is the wicket England needed. Surely that will see them over the line now. 
 246 21 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 WICKET published at 44.2 overs 44.2 overs 
 Rathnayake c Baker b Dawson 118 (SL 329-8) 
 Four and out - a huge wicket for Liam Dawson!
 The England spinner removes centurion Pavan Rathnayake, who had swept the opening ball of the over past both Sam Curran and Will Jacks for a boundary at backward square.
 Rathnayake pulls out the sweep to the following delivery and top-edges a catch to Sonny Baker at short fine leg.
 Lucky it wasn't Jordan Cox who needed to take the catch, as he had no idea where the ball had gone.
 England firmly in control now.
 600 16 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 SL 325-7 published at 44 overs 44 overs 
 Need 62 from 36 balls 
 Well, Pavan Rathnayake is on strike now anyway, and he sends the next ball for four through backward point.
 Just one further single off the rest of the over though, with new batter Eshan Malinga facing two balls.
 The required run-rate leaps above 10 an over.
 50 6 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 15:54 GMT 15:54 GMT 
 Alex Hartley 
Former England bowler on Test Match Special 
 Sam Curran didn't take the stumps! 
 If he had done, then Pavan Rathnayake would have been out because they didn't cross!
 What was Curran waiting for? Rathnayake would have been out.
 When a game is on a knife edge, those are the little mistakes as to why England have not been winning games of cricket. 
 157 204 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 WICKET published at 43.2 overs 43.2 overs 
 Wellalage run out (Root/Curran) 1 (SL 320-7) 
 Image source, Getty Images It's Dunith Wellalage who goes - he'd walked off anyway, but I'm sure England would have preferred Pavan Rathnayake.
 Wellalage pushes to backward point, Rathnayake runs through even though his partner doesn't move.
 The throw comes to Sam Curran and he strolls over to the stumps before finally taking off the bails.
 The question is, had Curran broken the stumps earlier might he have removed Rathnayake instead? 
 We would have to had seen if Rathnayake had passed Wellalage at that point.
 212 24 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Umpire review published at 43.2 overs 43.2 overs 
 It's a wicket... but who's going?
 Both Sri Lanka batters end up at the striker's end, with Sam Curran taking off the bails.
 It's unclear which batter has gone here, the umpires are taking a look.
 137 20 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 15:53 GMT 15:53 GMT 
 Alex Hartley 
Former England bowler on Test Match Special 
 Mistakes like that for England could be costly. 
 Gus Atkinson in the deep there sliding past the ball and it goes through him. 
 England have got to be on their A game here in the last seven overs of this game. 
 37 33 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 SL 320-6 published at 43 overs 43 overs 
 Need 67 from 42 balls 
 Dunith Wellalage comes in at eight and gets Pavan Rathnayake on strike with a single sent square from his second delivery.
 Rathnayake cracks Henry Crocombe's final delivery to the ropes at cover point, where a sliding Gus Atkinson maybe should have done a bit better stopping the ball - that's four.
